claims.text: The applicable alloy is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The starting alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
The starting state has high plasticity and machinability but low hardness and strength.
Relatively facile dislocation glide governs the low hardness and strength.
The starting solid solution has limited lattice distortion.
The starting solid solution lacks strong solute-dislocation interactions.
Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti have sufficiently similar atomic sizes and bonding characteristics to provide few obstacles to dislocation motion in this alloy.
Ti has only a small-fraction effect on lattice strain and dislocation resistance in this alloy.
A controlled heat treatment can induce slight solute segregation or nanoscale clustering while avoiding significant secondary-phase formation.
Nanoscale solute clusters or incipient precipitates act as dislocation-pinning centers.
Increased dislocation pinning from nanoscale chemical heterogeneity raises hardness and yield strength.
Minimal solute-dislocation interaction enables easy glide and dynamic recovery during deformation.
Relative to the heat-treated clustered variant, the as-cast alloy will have lower yield strength and hardness under identical testing.
The as-cast alloy will show wide glide bands and lower dislocation accumulation, indicating relatively unimpeded glide.
TEM of the heat-treated variant will reveal dislocations pinned at nanoscale clusters.
The comparison should hold grain size and general microstructural uniformity comparable between the as-cast and heat-treated samples.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to ambient-temperature, quasi-static to moderate-strain-rate loading.
The proposed mechanism assumes that processing does not form significant secondary phases.
The mechanism may cease to apply at high temperature or when grain growth or extensive precipitation causes major microstructural evolution.

contradictions.description: The alloy is described as equimolar or nearly equimolar, which makes Ti approximately 20 at.% rather than a small fraction; the mechanism nevertheless invokes a 'small fraction effect from Ti.'

The strengthening mediator includes 'incipient precipitates,' while the processing and applicability conditions require clustering or ordering without forming a second phase. Whether incipient precipitates satisfy that restriction is left inconsistent or ambiguous.
